headline: Laws are formalized rules—agreements about behavior that carry consequences for violation
universal_truth: Rules exist because groups need coordination; laws are how societies agree on shared expectations
fun_facts: The oldest known written laws are the Code of Ur-Nammu, from around 2100-2050 BCE
Laws differ from customs in having formal enforcement mechanisms
Every society has rules, though what's legal varies enormously across cultures and time
discussion_questions: When is it right to break an unjust law?
How do laws differ from customs or social norms?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Groups need rules. When everyone just does whatever they want, chaos results. Laws are formalized rules—written, public, enforced. They're how societies agree on what's acceptable and what's not.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why do we need formal laws? Why not just rely on custom and social pressure?

options.text: Laws provide clarity and consistency—unwritten rules are interpreted differently; laws make expectations explicit, apply equally to all, and provide predictable consequences
options.response: Yes. Laws remove ambiguity. Everyone knows what's expected. Consequences are predictable. This creates the stability needed for complex society—you can plan when you know the rules.
They do restrict some behaviors, but they also enable others—contracts, property, safety require law...

q1.title: Laws Enable Freedom
q1.script: Paradoxically, laws create freedom. Without laws against theft, you can't securely own. Without contract law, you can't reliably trade. Restriction and enablement are intertwined.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Laws Enable Freedom"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Legitimate vs Imposed
q2.script: Not all laws are legitimate. Laws can be unjust. The key question: Did affected people have voice in creating the law? Law imposed without consent differs from law created together.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Laws Change
q3.script: What's legal changes. Slavery was legal. Women voting was illegal. Laws evolve as understanding grows. Bad laws can and should be changed through legitimate process.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Rules exist because groups need coordination. Laws are how societies agree on shared expectations. Understand and participate in rule-making.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 335—December begins! Tomorrow, we'll explore rules everyone agrees on—social contracts. Until then, consider what makes a law legitimate.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Law Reflection - What Rules Shape Your Life?
growTrack.learning_objective: Understand law's role in daily life
growTrack.activity: What laws affect your daily life? Which do you follow automatically? Which do you question? Are there laws you think should change? How might you participate in changing them?
